stem:
This excerpt is from a presidential address from the 1920s.

Which statements highlight President Warren G. Harding’s domestic economic policies after World War I?

Select TWO choices that correctly answer the question.
instruction: Select TWO choices that correctly answer the question.

options.label: A
options.text: America is ready to encourage, eager to initiate, anxious to participate in any seemly program likely to lessen the probability of war. . . .

options.label: B
options.text: I speak for administrative efficiency, for lightened tax burdens . . . for the omission of unnecessary interference of Government with business. . . .

options.label: C
options.text: I wish for an America no less alert in guarding against dangers from within than it is watchful against enemies from without. . . .

options.label: D
options.text: . . . Opportunity is calling not alone for the restoration, but for a new era in production, transportation and trade. . . .

options.label: E
options.text: . . . Believing in our higher standards, reared through constitutional liberty and maintained opportunity, we invite the world to the same heights.

visual_elements: President Warren Harding’s inaugural address, March 4, 1921
